title: Separate warm and cold slopes gave no clear next-winter Nino 3.4 forecast gain in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether separate warm and cold slopes improve next-winter Nino 3.4 forecasts beyond a linear model with the current and previous winter. We used a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 monthly anomaly record. Each fit used earlier years only. In 45 target winters, 1981-2025, the added absolute-value term reduced mean squared error by 10.54%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -4.48% to 24.69%. The evidence gives no clear mean gain and does not rule one out. Error reduction was -5.54% for Nino 3 and 4.70% for Nino 4. A symmetric square term gave a 5.06% gain in Nino 3.4. Small samples, revised source data, a fixed later reference period, simple model form and conditional intervals limit inference. This is a retrospective forecast benchmark, not a causal test or an operational forecast. The package gives annual inputs, code, all forecasts, block draws, a figure, source hashes and an independent numerical audit.
